reason: The cited evidence shows that lattice distortion and SRO affect dislocation behavior in HEAs (E1, E2) and that SRO and lattice distortion are inversely coupled (E3), but none of the passages address multilayer interfaces, creep mechanisms, or the specific interplay between diffusion and dislocation activity under sustained loading. The key premises about interface-mediated gradients and the creep transition are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: SRO and lattice distortion vary spatially in HEA multilayers
SRO and lattice distortion control differential dislocation nucleation and mobility at interfaces
Stronger SRO impedes dislocation glide, weaker SRO allows easier motion
This leads to a gradient of plastic deformation and a transition from diffusion- to dislocation-mediated creep
HEA multilayers will show a gradual increase in dislocation density and strain gradient, unlike conventional multilayers
